title: Rabbi Shila (a Tanna of the Tosefta)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Tosefta Kelim 4:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Kelim_Kamma.4.9), Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel transmits a teaching in Rabbi Shila’s name.

He is likewise mentioned in [Tosefta Berakhot 2:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Berakhot.2.9), with a parallel in [Sukkah 26a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.26a.1): “Our Rabbis taught … in the name of Rabbi Shila they said: A bridegroom is exempt,” etc.

In [Taanit 11a](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.11a.8-10): “Our Rabbis taught: When Israel is in distress … those of the school of Rabbi Shila said: Two ministering angels,” etc. … “they testify against him … Rabbi Chidka says.”
He is likewise mentioned in the Mekhilta, Beshalach, parashah Vayassa, chapter 1 (Hyman’s numbering; compare [2:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Mekhilta_DeRabbi_Yishmael%2C_Tractate_Vayassa.2.5)).

Hyman concludes from all these places that he lived still in the generation of Rabban Gamliel. He suggests that the Rabbi Shila in the incident cited in [Berakhot 58a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.58a.13-14) is the Tanna.[^4] He recounts the episode as follows: Rabbi Shila flogged a certain man who had relations with a gentile woman. He went and informed on him to the king (in Dikdukei Soferim, in one manuscript, it reads “informed on him to the Caesar’s house”), that he was judging cases without the king’s authority. They sent an officer after him and asked him: “Why did you flog this man?” He said: “Because he had relations with a donkey.” “Do you have witnesses?” He said, “Yes.” Eliyahu came and testified. They said: “If so, he is liable to death.” He said: “Since the day we were exiled from our land we have no authority to kill.” While they sat examining his case, Rabbi Shila opened and said: “Yours, Lord, is the greatness,” etc. They said to him: “What are you saying?” He said: “Thus I am saying: Blessed is the Merciful One, who gave a kingdom on earth like the kingdom of heaven, and gave you dominion and love of justice.” They said: since the honor of the kingdom is so dear to him, they gave him a staff and appointed him a judge (at the gate of Rome — Dikdukei Soferim). And that man asked him …

notes.text: Supplied ושאלו ההוא breaks off mid-sentence; p005 remains held, without completing Hyman from Berakhot. וכן/נגד/גברא readings disclose the draft’s ובן/ננד/נברא. Preserve every quoted dialogue, royal authority, staff, appointment, DikdukeiSoferim gloss and Hyman’s tentative Tanna identification.

The supplied text breaks off at the end of p. 1111. Hyman’s printed entry (vol. III, p. 1112) continues: The man he had flogged asked, “Does God perform a miracle for a lie?” Shila replied, “Wicked man! Are they not called donkeys?” Rabbi Shila saw that the man meant to denounce him for calling them donkeys. He declared him a pursuer, struck him with the staff and killed him, and then expounded the verse “Yours, Lord, is the greatness.” The next heading starts a separate entry for Rav Shila. This note supplies Hyman’s printed continuation. The consulted Berakhot 58a gives a fuller account.

The Tosefta citation is Kelim Kamma 4:9. Rabbi Shila’s saying about sixty-one meals appears in chapter 1 of Vayassa in the consulted Wikisource arrangement and at Vayassa 2:5 in the consulted Sefaria editions. The printed Hyman reads וכן, נגד and גברא where the supplied text gives ובן, ננד and נברא. The Dikdukei Soferim variants are reported by Hyman, whose identification of the Rabbi Shila in this story remains a suggestion.

[Vayassa 2:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Mekhilta_DeRabbi_Yishmael%2C_Tractate_Vayassa.2.5) attributes the count of sixty-one meals to Rabbi Shila. The corresponding [Seder HaDorot entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3287&lang=en) also recounts the trial and reports that Yuchasin ascribes the story to Rabbah bar Shila. Hyman only suggests identifying the Rabbi Shila in this episode with the Tanna.
